summary:
I measured shape targets from 9 photos of the real boat and compared them with baseline_fine.stl. All work is in scratchpad/v10/photo; the repo and worktrees were not touched. 46 targets are in targets.json, with value, unit, uncertainty, source image, method and today's model value.

**How each photo was calibrated**
- **IMG_9370 (side):** fitted an orthographic camera with roll, yaw and elevation. Calibrated on the drawing's stem profile (rms 0.7 px), the stem head at z=1204 and the rub-rail line strake_z (rms 1.0 px, about 10 mm). The image turned out isotropic (9.56 x 9.89 mm/px). The fitted 7° camera elevation is doubtful, because the coachroof roof is not visible. Gaps measured on the hull side (window, rail, deck edge) do not depend on it.
- **IMG_9388 (bow head-on):** fitted a pinhole camera (f=1888 px, 1.47 m ahead of the bow) to the rub-rail silhouette, the stem line and the keel. The rail fit is rms 5-9 px and the keel tip is 44 px off, so absolute numbers here carry ±40 mm.
- **IMG_9391 (transom):** a pinhole camera fit failed (rail rms 13 px), so I used scale-free ratios instead (±0.08).
- **Deck photos (IMG_9304, IMG_9372):** mostly qualitative, because of perspective.

**Biggest differences from today's hull**
1. **Topsides.** Head-on, the real outline below the rail stays out. Flare is about 5° just under the rail and grows to about 15° 0.45 m lower, so the side is convex. It lies 33-37 px (1.1°) outside today's outline. That is about 95-110 mm more half-breadth at z 270-440 near x≈3550. Today's side is hollow right under the rail. This supports the convex section family from the sections lens.
2. **Rub rail.** The real rail is a dark D-profile about 45 x 30 mm. It runs unbroken from the stem head round both stern quarters, with no flat end. Today's rail is a 95 x 55 square bar with a flat bow end and knuckles at the stern.
3. **Window.** The real window is about 1610 mm long (x≈4010-5620). Its frame is 255 mm tall with a raised rim about 25 mm wide, a semicircular forward end and a rounded aft end that leans forward at the top. Today's window is 3700-4900, 176 mm tall, with R55 corners. This conflicts with the 1:50 drawing, so it should be checked before the model is changed.
4. **Deck edge amidships.** The window frame top sits 315 mm above the rail centre, so the deck edge must be at least about 330 mm above the rail (today 271 mm). That means DECK_EDGE_Z should be at least about 1160 at x 4200-4800 (today 1099-1114), assuming strake_z is right. At the bow and the transom, the gap between the deck edge and the rail matches the drawing.
5. **Stern.** Seen from astern, the outline is a smooth convex U. The half-width at the boot-top is about 0.70 of the half-width at rail level; today it is about 0.84. The transom has no crease where it meets the sides, the boot-top is straight across the middle 55%, and the rail turns the corners smoothly.
6. **Stem and bow.** The stem is rounded, R≈30 mm; today it is a knife edge with a flat cap. The bow waterline at boot-top height is roughly today's, 10-45 mm fuller.
7. **Mast.** The side photo puts the mast at about 3600 ±120 mm from the bow; params.py has 3400. Worth checking.
8. **Boot-top.** The blue band is about 100 mm tall, with a cream pinstripe about 20 mm wide below it. Its top edge is about 120 mm above the waterline amidships and rises roughly 35 mm toward the ends.

model_vs_photo.today: Hollow under the rail: the outline pulls in right below the 95x55 rail, then runs straight; at x~3550, z 270-440 the half-breadth is 974-1011 mm
model_vs_photo.photo: Convex: flare ~5 deg under the rail growing to ~15 deg 0.45 m lower; outline 33-37 px (1.1 deg) outside today's, about +95-110 mm half-breadth at z 270-440 near x~3550
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Use the convex single-curve section (sections-6) with flare ~5-8 deg at rail height amidships and ~15 deg at z~300, at least +40 mm bulge over the chord. Then re-render with the IMG_9388 camera (B_bow overlay) and check the outline stays out below the rail

model_vs_photo.today: 95 x 55 square bar, ruled loft, flat end at x=200, 16-26 deg knuckles at the stern corner
model_vs_photo.photo: Dark D-profile ~45 mm tall, ~30 mm proud, rounded face; runs from the stem head under the bow roller, round both quarters and across the transom with smooth turns
model_vs_photo.suggestion: STRAKE_H~45, STRAKE_PROUD~30 (1.5 x 1.0 mm on the model) as a half-round/D profile; start it at the stem; densify the corner path; keep the centre on strake_z (it matches within 15 mm)

model_vs_photo.today: x 3700-4900 (1200 mm), 176 mm tall, R55 rounded rectangle, 15 mm recess
model_vs_photo.photo: x ~4010-5620 (1610 mm); frame 255 mm tall (glass 190), top 315 mm and bottom 55 mm above the rail centre; semicircular forward end, aft end rounded and leaning forward at the top (~85 mm); raised rim ~25 mm
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Check against the drawing first: it conflicts with the 1:50 tracing (3666-4841). If confirmed, lengthen and move the window aft, make the forward end a full semicircle, rake the aft end, and model the frame as a raised rim around a shallow recessed glass

model_vs_photo.today: DECK_EDGE_Z 1099-1114 at x 4200-4800, 271 mm above the rail centre
model_vs_photo.photo: Window frame top is already 315 mm above the rail centre, so the deck edge sits at least ~330 mm above it (z >= ~1160). Bow (90 mm) and transom (140 mm) gaps match the drawing
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Re-check the 1:50 tracing of the thin deck line between x~3000 and 6500. If the rail line is right, lift DECK_EDGE_Z by about 50-60 mm there with a smooth spline that keeps the bow and transom values; otherwise lower strake_z. Either way the window must sit inside the gap

model_vs_photo.today: Raked cambered face cut from a loft that runs straight aft; sharp face edge; astern outline nearly parallel then pinched (half-width at boot-top ~0.84 of rail level)
model_vs_photo.photo: Smooth convex U, no crease at the transom edge; half-width at boot-top ~0.70 of rail level; boot-top straight over the middle 55%, turning down round soft corners
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Narrow the aft waterline (as in sections-3, WL half-breadth at x 7000-7800 down 15-25%) and build the corner into the sections or the stern loft (R ~100-250 mm in plan at rail height, larger lower down) instead of a boolean face. Keep the deck outline and the 8-10 deg rake

model_vs_photo.today: Knife edge with a flat 174 x 9 mm cap at x=4
model_vs_photo.photo: Rounded stem, R ~30 mm (shading band 45-55 mm wide) along the whole visible stem
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Add the square-root foot from edges-9 with R~25-35 mm (about 1 mm on the model) and close the bow with the round nose
No change needed beyond noise. If anything, ease the entrance 10-40 mm fuller at x 1200 and 2400 when the sections are rebuilt
Cross-check against another photo or a tape measurement before moving the mast; the two disagree by about 1.5 sigma

model_vs_photo.photo: Blue band ~100 mm, cream pinstripe ~20 mm below it; top edge ~120 mm above the floating waterline amidships, rising ~35 mm toward the ends
model_vs_photo.suggestion: If wanted, a 0.1-0.2 mm deep emboss or a colour-change line: top at about DWL+100 amidships, sheered up 30-40 mm at the ends

model_vs_photo.today: Sprayhood a loaf with flat vertical ends that swallows D300 winches; anchor-roller brick; flat-topped coaming
model_vs_photo.photo: Sprayhood a soft dome with raked front and rounded aft hoop; small winches on the coaming clear of the hood; plough anchor on a slim bow roller; low coaming with rounded edges fading aft
model_vs_photo.suggestion: Follow edges-6/7/2/8: cap the hood ends, move the winches out, use a slim roller and fillet the coaming
